subject: Pinecrest — evidence packaging & technical acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Elena Morris <security@pinecrest.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pinecrest.com, audits@lockoak.io
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence packaging & technical acceptance criteria for SOC2/ISO review

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, our InfoSec team needs a compact evidence package and a short tech acceptance checklist for the SOC 2/ISO items that are in scope.

To keep procurement moving we'd prefer:  
- A control-to-evidence mapping (CSV/XLSX) that lists Redwood control IDs, assertion text, and the artifact filename you will supply.
- One consolidated ZIP (or Drive folder) with example artifacts (logs, policy PDFs, config screenshots) and a README describing each file.
- A brief technical acceptance checklist (1 page) that our engineers can run through during a 30–45 minute verification call.

Can you confirm format, a timeline (we need this by 2027-04-12 to keep our board approvals on schedule), and whether you can provide a sample bundle for internal review? Also loop in who on your side will own each artifact.

Best,
Elena Morris
Director, Information Security
Pinecrest Financial

Attachment: pinecrest-initial-scope.pdf (PDF stub)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <security@pinecrest.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence packaging & technical acceptance criteria for SOC2/ISO review

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Confirmed: we can deliver exactly the three items you outlined. Plan and immediate next steps below.

Deliverables (by 2027-04-12):
- redwood-control-map-pinecrest-v1.xlsx (control mapping with artifact name + owner)
- evidence-bundle-specification.pdf (README describing folder structure and redaction guidance)
- redwood-soc2-evidence-sample.zip (representative artifacts; redacted where needed)
- 1-page technical acceptance checklist (PDF)

Owners:
- Control mapping & checklist: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com)
- Evidence collection & packaging: Mina Haddad (mina_haddad@redwood.com)
- Technical walkthrough coordination & environment access: Soojin Lee (soojin_lee@redwood.com)

Notes on format and constraints:
- We will provide the mapping as XLSX with one row per control; each control will include columns for control text, evidence filename, collection method (screenshot/log/export), retention window, and any redaction notes.
- Artifacts will be provided via a Drive folder and a single ZIP for procurement. Sensitive logs will be redacted; we will include reproduction steps for any items that cannot be exported.
- For the acceptance checklist, we will provide a minimal runnable list: connectivity checks (IP allowlist), sample API call with headers, KV cache verification, and a log sampling procedure.

Can you confirm whether LockOak (audits@lockoak.io) should receive the bundle directly or if Pinecrest prefers to host the evidence in your secure intake? Also: do you need DocuSign PO before we hand over the bundle?

I'll upload draft artifacts to a shared Drive link and send you a DocuSign PO for your procurement team to sign.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-control-map-pinecrest-v1.xlsx (stub), evidence-bundle-specification.pdf (stub)

1) Marissa — finalize control mapping spreadsheet and link to existing SOC 2 controls. Target: 2027-04-06 EOD.
2) Mina — assemble redacted artifacts and build the ZIP + Drive layout. Target: 2027-04-09 so we can iterate with Elena.
3) Soojin — prepare the 1-page technical acceptance checklist and coordinate a 30–45 minute verification call. Target: 2027-04-08 (draft) and schedule call for 2027-04-13.

Constraints/Questions:

- Marissa, confirm if we should include both SOC 2 CC and ISO 27001 clause mappings in the same sheet (I think yes, two tabs).

Jonas

Jonas — confirmed. Quick answers:
- Sampling rules: for application logs, provide 7 days of redacted samples (every 6th file) plus an agreed-upon query to reproduce samples. For operational logs (infra), provide 24–72 hour windows with redaction.
- ISO + SOC2 mapping: yes, include both as separate tabs. I will draft the acceptance checklist (connectivity, sample API call, end-to-end request trace for a single token generation).

I'll send my draft checklist to the group by 2027-04-08 morning. Mina — let me know if you need help with redaction scripts; I have a small utility you can use.

Thanks,
Soojin
Principal Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
